glosses: to lay out (to arrange objects somewhere in a certain order, sequence, or to maintain their relation in space with each other)
to lay down, to lay out (to put someone in a horizontal position)
to lay out (to form a whole by placing a certain number of objects in a certain way)
to arrange, to set; to style (to cause something to take a certain physical shape)
to lay, to set (to cause the creation of specific text, work or intellectual product by combining certain elements)
to form, to shape, to train (to give things or behaviors a form that is considered good or at least acceptable)
to train (to teach the animal certain behaviors and skills)
to get comfortable (lying, to find a comfortable position)
to take on a particular shape
to occur, to unfold (to happen a particular way); (without an adverb); to work out, to pan out (to happen successfully)
to negotiate, to come to an agreement
